doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Emmett Hardy, Willie Guitar, Johnny Lala and others
summary: Short exchanges on Hardy's late arrival, Willie Guitar, Pete Dintram and Sbarbaro's cotton-mill boss, Lala.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: You remember Emmett Hardy, by the way?
Not too much. No, I think Emmett came after we left.
He came later, but then he died... After we left. You know, like old Girard. He died even faster than Girard. But I understand he played very well. No, those years I was out of town.
Yeah, that's what I wanted to establish. When did he come up? I don't know.
19... He didn't come maybe until around 1920s or so, like that.
Well, he must have really been brief then. He died in 25 or something. He died very fast. Like that, yeah.
Well, Girard didn't last for not too many years.
Yeah, I was at his funeral. Oh, did I happen to be passing then? They told me it was Girard's funeral and I stood by, yeah. Well, it was about two years ago.
I was working with him then.
